project.name: LAST SHIFT
project.workflow: one fresh OpenCode session per story

stories.title: Audit and stabilize the current repository
stories.objective: Inventory the partial project, preserve useful work, establish a clean baseline, and make the current project importable before adding features.
acceptance_criteria: Repository structure and current implementation state are documented in PROGRESS.md.
project.godot exists or is created with a valid main scene.
Broken references, parser errors, and obviously truncated files are identified.
The Godot executable is excluded from Git.
The global validation script succeeds, or the story is blocked with exact diagnostics.
No unrelated working code is discarded.

stories.title: Create the launchable project shell and title flow
stories.objective: Provide a stable title screen, New Game flow, placeholder level, pause flow, and return-to-title lifecycle.
acceptance_criteria: The project launches directly to a title screen.
New Game opens a playable placeholder level.
Pause and return-to-title work without duplicate nodes or stale state.
The UI is navigable by keyboard and mouse.
The project survives two consecutive title-to-game-to-title cycles.

stories.title: Implement responsive player movement
stories.objective: Implement a typed CharacterBody2D controller with acceleration, air control, variable jump, coyote time, jump buffering, dodge, one-way-platform drop-through, and stable respawn reset behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Horizontal acceleration and ground/air deceleration are distinct and configurable.
Variable-height jump, coyote time, and jump buffering behave correctly at edge boundaries.
Dodge has a cooldown and cannot leave the player permanently locked.
One-way-platform drop-through works.
Respawn clears velocity, transient timers, and movement state.
Movement parameters are centralized outside the controller where practical.

stories.title: Implement health, damage, death, and checkpoint respawn
stories.objective: Create reusable health and damage components with one-shot death, invulnerability windows, knockback metadata, and player checkpoint respawn.
acceptance_criteria: Damage data carries amount, type, source, hit position, direction, and knockback.
Entities cannot receive damage after death.
Death emits exactly once.
The player has post-hit invulnerability and visible feedback hooks.
Checkpoint respawn restores a valid controllable state.
Deterministic tests cover death-once and invulnerability behavior.

stories.title: Implement the weapon framework and pistol
stories.objective: Create a data-driven weapon interface and a functional pistol with independent aiming, safe muzzle handling, ammunition rules, recoil, and testable fire-rate logic.
acceptance_criteria: Mouse, right-stick, and keyboard fallback aiming are supported.
The pistol can fire in horizontal, vertical, and diagonal directions.
Muzzle obstruction prevents firing through walls.
Fire-rate restrictions cannot be bypassed by input spam.
Ammunition never becomes negative.
Weapon data is separated from player movement logic.

stories.title: Implement Shambler enemy, perception, and basic combat
stories.objective: Implement one complete zombie archetype with an explicit state machine, sight, line of sight, noise memory, pursuit, attack telegraph, damage, and death.
acceptance_criteria: The Shambler has explicit idle, investigate, chase, attack, stagger, and dead states.
Sight uses distance, field of view, and line-of-sight checks.
Gunfire noise can trigger investigation.
Last-known player position expires after a configurable duration.
Dead or inactive enemies stop receiving perception events.
The enemy can damage the player and be killed by the pistol.

stories.title: Build the first complete combat arena
stories.objective: Replace the placeholder level with a coherent traversal-and-combat arena containing platforms, hazards, a checkpoint, pickups, spawn points, and one optional side route.
acceptance_criteria: The player can traverse from entry to exit.
The arena contains static, one-way, and moving platforms.
At least one environmental hazard and one health or ammo pickup function.
Enemy spawn points are authored and categorized.
The checkpoint can be activated and used after death.
Traversal geometry is visually distinguishable from hazards and background.

stories.title: Add shotgun, rifle, melee, reload, and weapon switching
stories.objective: Extend the weapon framework with the remaining weapons, stable reload state, magazines, reserve ammunition, switching, recoil accumulation, and melee interruption.
acceptance_criteria: Shotgun pellet spread and knockback are functional.
The rifle supports automatic fire and recoil recovery.
Melee has a cooldown and can interrupt weak enemies.
Reload completion occurs exactly once.
Switching cannot bypass fire-rate or reload restrictions.
Weapon HUD data remains correct after switching and respawn.

stories.title: Add Runner, Spitter, Brute, and platform navigation
stories.objective: Implement three differentiated zombie archetypes and a pragmatic platform-aware navigation system with authored links, ledge safety, stuck recovery, and crowd separation.
acceptance_criteria: Runner, Spitter, and Brute have distinct state transitions and combat behavior.
Dangerous attacks are telegraphed.
At least one enemy can traverse an authored jump or drop link.
Enemies distinguish reachable, blocked, jump-required, drop-required, and unreachable targets.
Enemies avoid repeating impossible jumps indefinitely.
Crowd separation prevents exact positional stacking.

stories.title: Implement encounter director and final holdout
stories.objective: Create a deterministic threat-budget director, progressive encounter phases, recovery periods, safe spawn selection, enemy caps, and a final holdout encounter.
acceptance_criteria: The director tracks budget, enemy count, player condition, recent combat, and phase.
Spawn points on screen or too close to the player are rejected.
A deterministic seed reproduces spawn and phase decisions.
Pressure escalates while recovery periods remain possible.
Enemy count and budget caps are enforced.
The final holdout can reach a clear victory condition.

stories.title: Implement upgrades and deterministic choices
stories.objective: Create an upgrade system with random deterministic choices, stack limits, exclusions, gameplay effects, and an upgrade-selection UI.
acceptance_criteria: At least eight upgrades are defined as data.
Three choices are reproducible from a fixed seed.
Stack limits and mutually exclusive upgrades are enforced.
Descriptions show meaningful numerical effects.
Effects persist through checkpoint respawn.
Reloading a scene does not apply upgrades twice.

stories.title: Implement versioned save and load
stories.objective: Persist checkpoint, player state, weapons, ammunition, upgrades, completed encounters, deterministic seed, and relevant environment state using versioned safe data.
acceptance_criteria: New Game, Continue, restart from checkpoint, and clear-save flows work.
Save/load round trip preserves the required state.
Missing and corrupt files fall back safely.
Invalid values are sanitized.
Unknown fields do not crash loading.
The save format contains an explicit version.

stories.title: Complete HUD, feedback, audio architecture, and debug tools
stories.objective: Add production-readable HUD and menus, centralized feedback, managed audio emitters, performance counters, and isolated debug controls.
acceptance_criteria: HUD shows health, ammunition, weapon, reload, and encounter information.
Pause, death, victory, and options interfaces are functional.
Camera shake and hit stop combine predictably.
Transient audio and visual effects do not leak nodes.
The debug overlay exposes FPS, enemies, projectiles, director budget, player state, weapon state, checkpoint, and seed.
Debug actions can be disabled for a production build.

stories.title: Integration audit, tests, documentation, and release baseline
stories.objective: Perform a full integration pass, repair lifecycle defects, complete deterministic tests and documentation, and leave a runnable vertical slice with explicit known limitations.
acceptance_criteria: The project imports and starts without parser or missing-resource errors.
The title-to-game-to-victory loop is playable.
Core movement, weapons, enemies, director, upgrades, and saving are covered by automated or documented manual checks.
README.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, TESTING.md, and PROGRESS.md match the implementation.
No required feature is represented only by a deceptive placeholder.
Remaining defects and highest-risk files are explicitly documented.
